This is a Petition U/Sec. 22 of Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in accident occurred on 12.12.2018.

Sri vs Mr. Ramegowda on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30523030/
1 02.

The brief facts of the petitioner case is as follows:
2.1.
It is stated that, petitioner was working under respondents NO.1 .
The 1 st respondent is the owner of the Tipper Lorry and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of Tipper Lorry.

2.2. That on 12.12.2018 at about 5.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding on Tipper Lorry bearing No. KA-53-C-0165, at a little bit high speed, near Kateramma Temple,
Kundalahalli.

The BWSSB department was laying a pipeline under the road, when the said lorry ran over the said pipe, it was got broken and due to which the petitioner has lost control over the vehicle and Lorry has been capsized.
In the incident, right leg of the petitioner was trapped under the Lorry.
He sustained crush injury in right foot with 3 rd MT fracture, 1st and 2nd Toe vascular injury and other injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Vydehi Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Center, wherein first aid was given to him and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital for further treatment.

entities.text: Vydehi Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Center
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2.3. It is stated that, he has taken treatment as an inpatient in above hospital for 19 days.
During the hospitalization, surgery was done for all three fractures and fixed with implants.
After the discharge from the hospital, he has taken regular follow-up treatment as per the advise of the doctor and still he is under medical care and treatment.
2.4. The petitioner was aged about 40 years at the time of incident and he was getting salary of Rs.15,000/- per month with daily bata of Rs.100/-.
Due to injuries, he lost the earning capacity and became a disabled person.

The Airport Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.
No.117/2018 against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Sec.279, of IPC.
It is contended that petitioner was working as a driver in above Lorry and he was a permanent employee of the 1 st respondent.
2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Accordingly, petitioner prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
03. Despite due service of court notice respondent NO.1 has remained absent and therefore he has been placed ex- parte in the case.
04. Respondent No.2- Insurance Company has filed written statement contending that RC owner of the offending vehicle has violated Sec. 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act.
RC owner of the vehicle has allowed the petitioner to drive the vehicle knowing fully well that he had no valid DL.
The employer and employee relationship between the petitioner and respondent No.1 is denied.
The age and income of the petitioner is denied.
There is 7 days delay in lodging complaint with jurisdictional police.
The insurance company has denied the alleged accident and involvement of the vehicle.

It is contended that false complaint has been lodged with a police with an intention to get compensation from Sri vs Mr. Ramegowda on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30523030/
2 insurance company.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner and expenses incurred in medical treatment is denied.
The physical disability of the petitioner is denied.
It is contended that insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.
With these averments he prays to dismiss the petition.
05. On the basis of pleadings and documents of both parties the court has framed the following Issues:

:ISSUES:
1.

Whether petitioner proves that he comes within the purview of the word "employee"
under the provisions of the Employees Compensation Act?
2. Whether petitioner proves that he was labour and working as a driver under the respondent No.1.?

3. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained alleged injury in view of caused an accident which was occurred by vehicle bearing registration No. KA-53-C-0165 on 12.12.2018 at about 05.00 a.m. near Kateramma Temple, Kundalahalli, during the course of his employment under 1st respondent?
4. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
5. What order or award?
06. In order to prove his case, Petitioner was examined as Pw.1 and one witness was examined as P.W.2 and exhibits were marked as Ex.P:1 to 13.

Learned counsel for respondents has cross examined P.W.1 and 2.
07.
The insurance company has examined Record Clerk, RTO and legal Officer as R.W.1 and 2 respectively.
Exhibits were marked as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.6.
Counsel for Petitioner has cross-examined R.W.1 and R.W.2.
08. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner.
Counsel for respondent NO.2 has field written arguments.
Perused the oral and documentary evidence placed by both parties.

09. My findings to the above referred Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 :- In the affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the affirmative.
Issue No.3 :- In the affirmative.
Issue No.4 :- In partly affirmative.
Issue No.5 :- As per final order for the  following.

:REASONS:

3 10. ISSUE No. 1 and 2:- To avoid repetition of facts and for sake of convenience, the above Issues are discussed together here under:
11.
Employer and employee relationship:-
Insurance Company has denied the employer and employee relationship between the respondent No.1 and the petitioner.
It is the burden of the petitioner to prove the employer and employee relationship and he was working as a driver under respondent No.1.
It is significant to note that,
respondent No.1, the R.C. owner of the vehicle has not contested the case and he has been placed Ex-parte in this case.
Respondent No.1 has not been challenged the employer and employee relationship.
12. The incident was occurred on 12.12.2018 at 5.00 a.m., on main road near Kundalahalli, Kateramma Temple.
One Murali son of Chinnaswamy Reddy, the writer of ASR Blue Metals Transport has lodged the complaint with the police regarding the alleged incident on 19.12.2018.
The incident was took place due to rash and negligent driving of the injured as per Ex.P.2-the Complaint.
In complaint it is clearly stated that, injured was the driver of A.S.R. Blue Metals Transport since 2 years.
13. The injured was transporting M. Sand on lorry at the time of accident and it is evident from perusal of Ex.P.2.
Perusal of Ex.P.6-the Charge Sheet also reveals that, injured was the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-C- 0165.
On the date of accident, the injured got admitted to the Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, at 12.27 p.m., with history of RTA.
In Ex.P.7, it is clearly mentioned that, injured was driving aforesaid Tipper Lorry at the time of accident.
14. Petitioner has produced D.L. to show his profession.
All these documents are sufficient to believe that, injured was the driver of respondent No.1, who is the R.C. owner of said Tipper Lorry.
Admittedly
Insurance Company has cross-examined P.W.1 in detail, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of witness to establish that, injured is not the employee of respondent No.1.

One of the employee of aforesaid transport has lodged complaint to the concerned P.S., regarding the incident stating that, petitioner is their employee and he has met with road traffic accident while driving the vehicle in question.
Hence, Issue No.1 and 2 are answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.3:-
To prove the incident, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of evidence.

In evidence he has deposed that, on 12.12.2018, he was driving the vehicle in question and at about 5.00 a.m., near Kateramma Temple he met with an accident as he lost control over the vehicle when the lorry was ran over the pipes laid by BWSSB Department.

To prove his case he has produced true copy of FIR in Cr.No.117/2018, Complaint, Spot Panchanama,
Hand Sketch Map of accident, IMV Report, Charge Sheet, Wound Certificate, Discharge Summary,
D.L., and 3 photographs at Ex.P.1 to 9.
Sri vs Mr. Ramegowda on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30523030/
4 16.

On the basis of complaint lodged by writer of aforesaid Transport Company, the Jurisdictional police have registered the case, proceeded with the investigation and submitted the charge sheet against the petitioner herein for the offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC.
17.

The reports prepared by Investigating Officer and Medical Reports issued by the Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedic are sufficient to believe the alleged accident and involvement of the vehicle.

The petitioner has produced true copy of M.V. Report of the vehicle in question at Ex.P.5.
18.
First of all, in this case, involvement of the vehicle in the accident is not in dispute at all.
The date and time of accident is not in dispute at all.

Admittedly, delay has been occurred in lodging the complaint with the police regarding the accident, but it is significant to note that, petitioner was severely sustained injuries in the incident and he was taking treatment in hospital as an inpatient.
Soon after the accident, he was shifted to Vydehi Institute of Medical Science and Research Center at While Field and it is evident from perusal of Ex.P.10-The Inpatient Bill.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Later, he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics for advanced treatment and it is evident from perusal of Ex.P.11-E.R. Record, Wound Certificate -Ex.P.7, final billing sheet- Ex.P.12.
19.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is the duty of the concerned hospital to give intimation to the Jurisdictional P.S., regarding MLC.
However, neither Vydehi Institute of Medical Science and Research Center, nor Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics have given MLC intimation to the jurisdictional P.S.

sentences.text: Therefore, delay of 7 days in lodging complaint to the police concerned is not a ground to doubt the case of the petitioner.

20. The oral evidence of P.W.1 and documents placed on record reveals that, petitioner had lost control over the vehicle, resulting in which lorry was capsized and his right leg was trapped under the said vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.3 is answered in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.4:- It is case of the petitioner that, he was hale and healthy prior to the accident and now, he cannot walk, stand for a long time as earlier due to the injuries sustained in RTA.
P.W.1 deposed that, he cannot climb or down stairs, fold his right leg, sit crossed leg and he cannot use Indian Toilet nor he wear slippers as before.
P.W.1 deposed that, he gets severe pain in the fracture site and a permanent scar has been remained over the operated part in the body.
He lost earning capacity due to the permanent disability suffered to.

22. Insurance Company has examined Santhosh Kumar, Record Clerk, RTO Office, Krishnagiri,
Tamilnadu as R.W.1 and produced Ex.R.1 to 4 through this witness.
Ex.R.1 is the Authorization Letter issued by RTO, Hosuru.
Ex . R.2
is the D.L. Extract of petitioner and perusal of same reveals that, his D.L. has been renewed even after the accident.
Ex.R.3 is the medical certificate issued by the Civil Surgeon, Hosuru certifying that, petitioner is physically fit to drive the vehicle.
Perusal of Ex.R.4-Form No.4 of injured issued by RTO office, Hosuru.

23. To establish the physical disability, petitioner has examined P.W.2-Dr. Prakashappa T.H.,
Orthopedic Surgeon of Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The medical witness Sri vs Mr. Ramegowda on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30523030/
5 has deposed that, on 12.12.2018, he has examined the injured with history of RTA and he found following injuries:
(I) Crush injury in right foot with near auto amputation of I and II Toe with fracture III M.T. of right foot.
The medical witness deposed that, X-ray of the wound was taken, POP Slab was applied and the patient was prepared for surgery.
Ex. P.11 is the E.R. Record of injured.

Oral evidence of P.W.2 and perusal of Ex.P.11 reveals that, on 13.12.2018, under S.A. amputation of I and II Toe and debridement of wound was done and then on 21.12.2018, under S.A. the Raw area over the right foot was covered with skin graft and then patient was discharged from the hospital on 31.12.2018 with an advise to continue with follow-up treatment.
24.

Medical witness has deposed that, he has examined the injured clinically and radiologically,
recently on 13.07.2021 to assess physical disability of the injured.
According to medical witness, the injured has sustained disability to the extent of 17% to the right lower limb and total amount of disability to the whole body from right lower limb is 9%.

He has produced X-ray film of the injured at Ex.P.13.
25.
Insurance Company has cross-examined P.W.2 in detail.
It is admitted fact that, right toe of the injured has been removed as he had sustained crush injury.
Evidence of P.W.2 reveals that, he has treated the injured and he was one of the medical expert in the medical team who have given treatment to the injured.
In cross-examination P.W.2 deposed that, the injured can drive the vehicle with little physical difficulties.
26. The petitioner has produced photographs of his right leg and the part of the leg removed off in the surgery at Ex.P.10.
The petitioner is a driver by profession and therefore, physical fitness and perfect legs plays a very important role in performing his duty.
After the surgery and specifically removal of his two toes, he cannot drive the vehicle as perfectly as before.
Any owner of vehicle may fear to give him vehicle to drive or engage him as their driver.
27. As far as age of the petitioner is concerned, he has stated that he was 40 years old at the time of the accident.
The petitioner has produced his D.L. at Ex.P.9, in which the date of birth is shown as 01.01.1975.
The incident was occurred on 12.12.2018.
Therefore, age of the petitioner is considered as 43 years at the time of incident on the basis of available record.

28. As far as the income of the petitioner is concerned, it is an admitted fact that the petitioner has not produced any convincing evidence to show that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month and daily bata at Rs.100/-.
On considering the age, avocation and time of the incident, this tribunal considered the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.8,000/- per month.

29. As far as the injuries sustained by the petitioner is concerned, this Tribunal has come to conclusion that the petitioner has got permanent disability to the extent of 9% to the whole body and therefore, compensation has to be determined as per Sec. 4 (1) (b) of Schedule 4 of Workmen's Sri vs Mr. Ramegowda on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30523030/
6 Compensation Act 1923.
On calculation, the total amount of compensation comes to Rs.8,000/- X 172.52 X 60/100) = Rs.8,28,096/-.
The injured has suffered physical disability at 9%.
Hence, the calculation is Rs.8,28,096/- X 9%, which comes to Rs.74,528/-.
30. Medical Expenses:-
The petitioner has produced total 7 medical bills at Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.12 and perusal of same reveals that, he has spent Rs.3,586/- and Rs.14,084/- for his treatment.

Therefore,
Rs.17,670/- is awarded towards medical expenses.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.74,528/- + Rs.17,670/- = Rs.92,198/-.
31. Liability:-
R.W.2 Sujan V. Ullal, the Legal Officer of Insurance Company has produced Authorization Letter and Insurance Policy of vehicle in question at Ex.P.5 and 6.
The insurance coverage of vehicle in question was valid from 07.08.2018 to 06.08.2019.

At the time of accident,
insurance of the vehicle in question was valid and effective.
Therefore, Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
32. Interest:-

The law is settled that, Employer is liable to pay the interest on the awarded amount and my reason is supported by the decision of hon'ble apex court reported in M.F.A no: 85/2013, in a case between New India Assurance Co. Ltd Vs Lilla Francis and others, Hon'ble high court of Kerala.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd Vs Lilla Francis and others, Hon'ble high court of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above decision insurance company is not liable to pay the interest on award amount.
The respondent no:1-the employer is liable to pay interest from the date of accident till the date of deposit at the rate of 12% as ordered by the Commissioner.
33. Jurisdiction: There is no objection regarding territorial jurisdiction of this commissioner to try the petition.
Both respondents have not raised any objection regarding jurisdiction to try the petition.
Therefore, this commissioner got jurisdiction to try the petition.
Therefore, Issue no:4 is answered in partly affirmative.

34. ISSUE No.5:- In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec. 22 of Employee's Compensation Act is hereby allowed in part.
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.92,198/-. (Rupee Ninety Two Thousand One Hundred and Ninety Eight).
The respondent no:1-the employer is liable to pay interest from the date of accident at the rate of 12% till the date of deposit of the compensation amount in the court as ordered by Commissioner.
The scheme of investment is dispensed with as the amount awarded is meager one.

Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-

7 Draw Award accordingly.
